judgments.yea_description: Voted for House Bill 5707. It would let a landowner dig or build a pond of less than 1 acre on land zoned for homes or farming without a state permit, if the pond is for noncommercial home use and is not connected to a lake, river or stream. The pond would also be exempt from the state's wetland permit rules, and the dug-out soil could be spread on nearby dry land. The exemption from the inland lakes and streams permit would reach back to January 1, 2020. The House passed it 63-44. The Senate has not voted on it, so it is not law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for House Bill 4445. It would let hunters bait deer anywhere in Michigan during the open deer seasons. Today a state wildlife order bans deer baiting in the Lower Peninsula. It would also write separate definitions of deer baiting and deer feeding into law. The House passed it 66-38. The Senate has not voted on it, so it is not law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for House Bill 5536. It would narrow which wetlands the state protects. A wetland would be covered only if it sits next to a federally protected water and has a continuous surface connection to it. Local wetland rules would keep the broader current test, except that a wetland could no longer qualify just by being larger than 5 acres. The House passed it 57-51. The Senate has not voted on it, so it is not law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for House Bill 5502. It would add to the list of wetlands the state does not regulate: any wetland created by accident through human activity that was not meant to create a wetland. The state environment department would have to prove a wetland was not created that way before regulating it. The House passed it 58-49. The Senate has not voted on it, so it is not law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for House Bill 5069. It would ban the sale of food containing brominated vegetable oil, propylparaben, or the dyes Red 40, Green 3, Blue 1, Blue 2 or Yellow 6, starting January 1, 2029. The ban would not apply if the federal government bans these substances by that date. The House passed it 56-51. The Senate has not voted on it, so it is not law.
